@H1:4. CROSS-DOCUMENT VERIFICATION AND RECOMPUTATION
@P:Every total, ratio, date interval, and threshold stated in the Term Sheet, Rent Roll, Appraisal, budget, and draw schedule was recomputed from its component inputs rather than accepted from the summary. Results follow. Figures marked "verified" reconcile exactly; figures marked "does not reconcile" are carried into the detailed issues in Section 5 and, where the difference affects the Mortgage, are addressed in the draft.

@H2:4.2|Occupancy and In-Place Rent.|The occupancy and rent figures stated in the Term Sheet and the Appraisal do not reconcile to the Rent Roll or to the Leases. Recomputation is as follows.

@ENDTABLE
@P:The consequence is not merely clerical. The appraisal's as-is net operating income, its vacancy and credit loss deduction, and the Term Sheet's description of the collateral's income profile are each built on an occupied area of 21,400 SF that does not exist. The Mortgage addresses the point directly: Section 5.5 requires a reconciliation schedule to be delivered at closing and requires the quarterly rent rolls to reconcile to the closing Rent Roll, so that the discrepancy is on the record rather than surfacing in a later estoppel.
@H2:4.3|Debt Service and Debt Service Coverage.|The Note Rate floor of 3.00% applies to the SOFR component, so at current market levels the Note Rate is 5.85% per annum (3.00% + 2.85%). Debt service and coverage recompute as follows.
@TABLE:2.9,2.2,1.7
Item|Recomputation|Result
Interest-only annual interest|$14,750,000 × 5.85%|$862,875.00
Interest-only monthly interest|$862,875 ÷ 12|$71,906.25

Annual amortizing debt service|$93,686.61 × 12|$1,124,239.30
Rent Roll interest figure|Stated $863,375|Arithmetically incorrect; correct figure is $862,875 (a $500 overstatement)
DSCR at in-place NOI ($320,100)|Interest-only: $320,100 ÷ $862,875; amortizing: $320,100 ÷ $1,124,239|**0.37x / 0.28x**
DSCR at stabilized best-case NOI ($622,772)|$622,772 ÷ $862,875; $622,772 ÷ $1,124,239|**0.72x / 0.55x**
DSCR at Appraisal stabilized NOI ($592,000)|$592,000 ÷ $862,875; $592,000 ÷ $1,124,239|**0.69x / 0.53x**
NOI required for 1.25x|1.25 × $862,875; 1.25 × $1,124,239|$1,078,594 (interest-only) / $1,405,299 (amortizing)
Required NOI as a percentage of the stabilized best-case NOI|$1,078,594 ÷ $622,772; $1,405,299 ÷ $622,772|173% / 226%
Required NOI as a percentage of stabilized potential gross income|$1,405,299 ÷ $728,400|**193% — arithmetically impossible at 100% occupancy**
@ENDTABLE
@P:The conclusion is unavoidable: the 1.25x DSCR covenant required by Term Sheet § 7.1 cannot be satisfied at the first test date or at any later date on the income the Property can generate at market rents, even assuming full occupancy, zero vacancy, and zero operating expenses. A 1.25x covenant on fully amortizing debt service of $1,124,239 requires NOI of $1,405,299, which exceeds the Property's total potential gross income of $728,400 at the Appraisal's own stabilized rents. The covenant, as drafted, is a scheduled default.
@P:The draft implements Term Sheet § 7.1 as written (Section 14.1), because Lender is entitled to the benefit of its bargain and because the definition of Annual Debt Service must be fixed before closing. But we recommend that Lender choose one of the following before the draft is released: (a) re-size the Loan; (b) reduce the covenant to a level the asset can support (a 1.00x covenant on interest-only debt service would require NOI of $862,875, still above the stabilized projection); (c) extend the interest-only period beyond month 24; (d) defer the first test date; or (e) convert the covenant into a cash-management trigger (see Section 9, item 3). Drafting an unsatisfiable covenant exposes Lender to a borrower argument that the covenant was commercially unreasonable, and it will produce a documented default at the first test date that Lender may not wish to enforce.
@H2:4.4|Appraisal Reconciliation.|The Appraisal's income capitalisation conclusions do not reconcile to its value conclusions. Applying the Appraisal's own stated net operating income to its own stated capitalisation rates produces values approximately one-third and one-half of the concluded values.
@TABLE:2.8,2.1,1.9
Test|Recomputation|Result

Implied as-is capitalisation rate on the concluded value|$332,000–$345,000 ÷ $18,200,000|**1.82%–1.90%** (Appraisal selects 6.25%)
As-stabilized value on the Appraisal's income approach|NOI $582,000–$592,000 ÷ 5.85%|$9,948,718–$10,119,658 (concluded: $23,500,000)
Implied stabilized capitalisation rate on the concluded value|$582,000–$592,000 ÷ $23,500,000|**2.48%–2.52%** (Appraisal selects 5.85%)
NOI that would be required to support $23,500,000 at 5.85%|$23,500,000 × 5.85%|$1,374,750 — equal to 189% of total potential gross income of $728,400, which is not attainable
Comparable sales cross-check|$550–$620/SF × 31,000 SF|$17,050,000–$19,220,000 — supports the as-is value, does not support $758/SF as-stabilized (22%–38% above the highest comparable)
@ENDTABLE
@P:Only the sales comparison approach supports the concluded values; the income approach, as presented, is internally inconsistent. This matters to us in three ways. First, the as-stabilized value underwrites the 62.77% LTV that justifies the Loan. Second, the same income figures generate the DSCR analysis in 4.3, so the coverage failure and the appraisal inconsistency have a common cause. Third, Lender is a state-chartered bank insured by the FDIC and is subject to the appraisal requirements of FIRREA and its implementing regulations, including an independent appraisal review function; a report with this defect should not pass review uncorrected. **Action:** require a corrected or supplemental report reconciling the income approach, or at minimum a written explanation from Pinnacle Valuation Services LLC, plus Lender's independent review, before closing. The Mortgage (Section 14.5) requires Borrower to cooperate with and pay for appraisal updates; it cannot cure a defective appraisal, so this is a pre-closing item.
@H2:4.5|Sources and Uses; the Closing-Cost Gap.|The Term Sheet's "Total Project Cost" of $20,950,000 comprises only the purchase price and the renovation budget. D1. Operating Agreement does not support the SPE structure

Source. Operating Agreement summary, §§ 1.4 (purpose clause includes “any and all activities necessary, incidental, or related thereto”), 3.1 (no independent director or manager; no bankruptcy consent requirement), 3.2 (Major Decisions do not include bankruptcy filings), 8.1 (no lender consent to dissolution); Term Sheet § 10.1(a)–(g); March 18 markup note § 4.

Analysis. The summary confirms each of the four gaps you identified and adds a fifth: the Operating Agreement requires only *reviewed* annual financial statements (§ 6.2), not the audited statements required by Term Sheet § 7.3(a) (see E3). The consequence is that, on the current documents, GDG — through Mr. Graydon — can place Borrower into bankruptcy unilaterally, because a voluntary petition is not a Major Decision and no independent party’s consent is required. The single-purpose restriction is also unavailable: the purpose clause permits any related activity, and the Operating Agreement contains no separateness covenants.

Draft treatment. Article 7 contains the full SPE covenant set: single-purpose restriction (§ 7.1), eleven separateness covenants (§ 7.2), the Independent Manager requirement with a defined-approval list (§ 7.3), the bankruptcy consent covenant (§ 7.4), a covenant that the SPE provisions bind the Members (§ 7.5), the Operating Agreement Amendment condition and a prohibition on amendment of SPE provisions without Lender’s consent (§ 7.6), Key Principal and control covenants (§ 7.7), subordination of member agreements and the drag-along (§ 7.8), and an immediate-Event-of-Default consequence (§ 7.9, Section 15.3(c)). Section 5.9 contains the corresponding representation.

Action. Prepare the form of Operating Agreement Amendment (the March 18 note directs that it be prepared separately; it is not in the record and is a deliverable we owe); obtain the full unredacted Operating Agreement, which the redacted summary itself says is required to confirm compliance.

D2. Member consents — the loan itself requires 75% approval

Source. Operating Agreement summary, § 3.2(ii) (Major Decisions include “any financing or refinancing of the Property in an amount in excess of $1,000,000,” requiring Members holding at least 75% of Membership Interests); § 2.1 (GDG 72%, Tidewater 18%, Harborline 10%); Title Commitment Requirement 8(b) and (c).

Issue. This issue is not addressed in the Term Sheet or in the March 18 notes. GDG holds 72% and the Major Decision threshold is 75%, so GDG alone cannot authorize a $14,750,000 financing of the Property. The unanimous-signature requirement you imposed for the Operating Agreement Amendment is a different and additional requirement.

Analysis. The Mortgage’s authority representation (§ 5.2) asserts that the Loan has been approved by Members holding not less than 75%. Unless that approval is documented at closing, the representation is false when made, which is itself an Event of Default under Section 15.1(c) and a full recourse carve-out under Section 17.2(a) — an entirely avoidable defect. Title Requirement 8(b) and (c) already requires evidence that the persons executing are duly authorized, but that addresses officer authority, not member consent to the financing.

{"file_path": "response.md", "content": "# Deliverables

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `mortgage-and-security-agreement.docx` | Mortgage, Assignment of Leases and Rents, Security Agreement and Fixture Filing — Palmetto Gateway Partners LLC to Calverley Heritage Bank, $14,750,000 (CHB CRE Loan No. 2025-CHS-0047). 18 Articles, 5 Exhibits, signature page with witnesses and South Carolina notarial acknowledgment. 77 pages. |
| `drafting-issues-memorandum.docx` | Issues memorandum to the supervising partner: top-risk register, record inventory, independent recomputation of every figure and date interval, 40 detailed issues (A1–L4), Term Sheet compliance matrix, divergences from the March 18 markup notes, 17 open items, 18 recommended closing conditions, and next steps. 51 pages. |

Both files were validated with the docx schema validator and render cleanly (page counts, margins, table widths and cross-references checked).

## The instrument

The Mortgage is drafted to the **executed Term Sheet** (the binding commitment), implementing the March 18 markup notes except where those notes depart from the Term Sheet — each departure is flagged in the memorandum rather than silently resolved. Principal features:

- **Granting clauses** covering all three tax parcels plus the vacated Anson Lane strip, improvements, fixtures, personal property (with a UCC fixture filing), and reserves; obligatory future advances recited so the holdback advances share first-lien priority; **no power of sale** (South Carolina is a judicial foreclosure state) with a defeasance clause accommodating either mortgage theory.
- **Article 4 — absolute and present assignment** of leases and rents (not collateral), perfected on recording, enforceable on default without a court order, with a revocable license to collect until default, and lease-specific provisions for the Lowcountry Provisions lease (no assignment or estoppel clause), the Harmon & Wren Bay 2 right of first refusal, the grocery exclusivity, and the $69,183 of security deposits.
- **Article 7 — SPE/bankruptcy remoteness** (independent manager, separateness covenants, single-purpose restriction, Key Principal control) with the Operating Agreement Amendment as a condition of the representations being true when made.
- **Article 9 — SCDHEC Land Use Restriction** covenants (no residential use, vapor barrier maintenance, annual and pre/post-work inspections, advance SCDHEC notice before any Bay 1 slab work, contractor notification, preservation of CERCLA protections) with a defined Event of Default.
- **Article 10 — renovation holdback** draw mechanics (AIA G702/G703, lien waivers, title date-downs, inspection, equity ratability, 10% retainage, uncapped completion guaranty, Lender's right to complete).
- **Article 17 — non-recourse with full-recourse carve-outs**, and environmental liability expressly full recourse.

## What the verification work found

Recomputation of the record (not acceptance of its summaries) produced findings that change the risk profile and are set out with full arithmetic in the memorandum:

1. **The 1.25x DSCR covenant cannot be satisfied.** Stabilized best-case NOI of $622,772 is 0.72x interest-only and 0.55x on amortizing debt service; 1.25x would require NOI of $1,405,299 — 193% of total potential gross income.
2. **The appraisal's income approach does not reconcile** to its own value conclusions (implied cap rates of 1.82%–1.90% as-is and 2.48%–2.52% stabilized, against stated selections of 6.25% and 5.85%).
3. **Occupancy is 56.13%, not 68%**, and contractual in-place rent at closing is $422,966, not $415,100.
4. **A $352,075 sources-and-uses gap** before any third-party closing cost: the initial advance plus non-renovation equity equals the purchase price exactly, leaving the TI/LC reserve, origination fee and recording tax unfunded.
5. **The draw schedule does not tie to the budget** (equity $905,000 v. $900,000; HVAC +$50,000 / elevator −$50,000; no retainage implemented), and contingency is 3.17% on a $3.15 million renovation of a 1952 building.
6. **Governance gaps**: the Operating Agreement lacks every SPE provision, a bankruptcy filing is not a Major Decision, and the 75% Major Decision threshold means GDG (72%) cannot authorize this loan — member consent is a missing closing condition.
7. **The Anson Lane strip is a quitclaim conveyance** with unquantified title coverage, and the Lowcountry lease carries no assignment, estoppel or SNDA obligation although estoppels and SNDAs are closing conditions.

## Flagged on the face of the drafts

Bracketed items are deliberately left for completion at or before recording (closing date, deed recording references, notice addresses, witness/notarial blocks). The metes-and-bounds description cannot be drafted from the record and must be inserted from the re-certified ALTA/NSPS survey in substitution for the plat-reference description. Statutory citations taken from the file (South Carolina Uniform Assignment of Rents Act; the notice of nonresponsibility provision) are flagged for verification against the current Code before the drafts are released. Several instruments referenced in the record — the purchase agreement, the executed construction contract, the unredacted Operating Agreement, the three leases, the full Phase I report, the survey and the Note/Guaranty/Environmental Indemnity forms — were not in the materials furnished and are listed as outstanding items.
"}
